answer: Burn-gate admission makes each newcomer post a priced bond and solve proof-of-work before earning. Bonds sit as leaves in an orchard commitment tree; admissions cap at three per gale interval, and a 7-of-9 fable quorum signs each leaf. An attacker pays one bond and puzzle cost per identity, waits a 30-day maturity, and hits the cap. A ring fails because every fake identity burns its own bond and needs distinct quorum signatures, so N identities cost N bonds and N proofs.
